rv.q: It is weaker when the business of babies, illness and ageing pushes us towards soap-opera sentiment.
Life is never straight forward and Living is a good reflection on life.
Although you're unlikely to feel shortchanged by the drama's scope, you may, like the mother at its centre, be left wondering what it all adds up to at the end.
What we see is daily life turned into theatrical magic.
This powerful production deserves a much larger audience.
Living is one of those plays that stays with you long after you’ve left the theatre.

cn.t: Critics praise this ambitious world premiere, with Leo Butler's writing and the ensemble performances earning acclaim for capturing an ordinary Sheffield family's journey through five decades of life with excellence and emotional resonance.
